# TwinCAT ENI — Configuration Reference

**Source file:** `TwinCAT_ENI.xml`
**Schema:** `EtherCATConfig.xsd`, `Version="1.3"` (ETG.2100)
**Contents:** one EtherCAT master, one slave (Xeryon drive), one cyclic task
**Purpose of this document:** a complete plain-language description of what this ENI configures, for use as a known-good reference when comparing against configurations generated by other masters.

---

## 1. Network identity

### Master

| Field | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Name | `Device 1 (EtherCAT)` | |
| Destination MAC | `01 01 05 01 00 00` | TwinCAT's standard EtherCAT destination |
| Source MAC | `4c ea 41 63 17 44` | the actual host NIC |
| EtherType | `a488` | little-endian on the wire = `0x88A4`, EtherCAT |

### Slave

| Field | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Name | `Box 1 (Drive)` | |
| `AutoIncAddr` | `0` | first physical node on the segment |
| `PhysAddr` | `1001` | station address assigned during Init→PreOp (`0x03E9`) |
| `Physics` | `YY` | both ESC ports are MII and in use |
| VendorId | `78` (`0x4E`) | Xeryon |
| ProductCode | `1` | |
| RevisionNo | `1` | |
| SerialNo | `0` | not checked |

The slave sits at auto-increment position 0, i.e. it is the **first and only** node, cabled directly to the host NIC. Entry is therefore via ESC port 0 by construction.

---

## 2. Process data

The drive uses a **fixed PDO structure** — both PDOs carry `Fixed="true"` and `Mandatory="true"`. There is no CoE, no DS402, and no runtime PDO remapping. The mapping is baked into the ESI and cannot be changed by the master.

### Sync Managers

| SM | Direction | ESC address | Length | ControlByte | Enabled |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SM0 | Outputs (master → drive) | `0x1000` | 20 bytes | `0x64` | yes |
| SM1 | Inputs (drive → master) | `0x1200` | 8 bytes | `0x20` | yes |

Only two Sync Managers are defined. There are **no mailbox Sync Managers**, which is consistent with a device that supports no CoE/EoE/FoE — the state machine goes straight to process data.

### FMMUs

| FMMU | Logical address | Length | Physical | Type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FMMU0 | `0x01000000` | 20 bytes | `0x1000` | write (outputs) |
| FMMU1 | `0x01000000` | 8 bytes | `0x1200` | read (inputs) |

Both FMMUs share the same logical base address. That is intentional: a single `LRW` datagram writes 20 output bytes and reads 8 input bytes through the same logical window.

### Output map — RxPDO `0x1600` "Position" (20 bytes, SM0)

| Byte | Size | Field | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–3 | 32 bit | Command | STRING (4 ASCII chars) |
| 4–7 | 32 bit | Target position | DINT |
| 8–11 | 32 bit | Speed | UDINT |
| 12–13 | 16 bit | Acceleration | UINT |
| 14–15 | 16 bit | Deceleration | UINT |
| 16 | 8 bit | Execute | BYTE |
| 17–19 | 24 bit | padding | — |

The `Command` field is the Xeryon ASCII command word (`DPOS`, `ENBL`, `INDX`, `SCAN`, `RSET`, …). `Execute` is the handshake byte.

### Input map — TxPDO `0x1A00` "Status" (8 bytes, SM1)

| Byte.bit | Field |
|---|---|
| 0–3 | Actual position (DINT, 32 bit) |
| 4.0 | Amplifiers enabled |
| 4.1 | End stop |
| 4.2 | Thermal protection 1 |
| 4.3 | Thermal protection 2 |
| 4.4 | Force zero |
| 4.5 | Motor on |
| 4.6 | Closed loop |
| 4.7 | Encoder index |
| 5.0 | Encoder valid |
| 5.1 | Searching index |
| 5.2 | Position reached |
| 5.3 | Error compensation |
| 5.4 | Encoder error |
| 5.5 | Scanning |
| 5.6 | Left end stop |
| 5.7 | Right end stop |
| 6.0 | Error limit |
| 6.1 | Searching optimal frequency |
| 6.2 | Safety timeout |
| 6.3 | Execute ack |
| 6.4 | Emergency stop |
| 6.5 | Position fail |
| 6.6–6.7 | padding (2 bit) |
| 7 | Slot (BYTE) |

`Execute ack` at 6.3 is the acknowledge half of the `Execute` handshake.

## 3. Distributed Clocks

```
<DC>
  <ReferenceClock>true</ReferenceClock>
  <CycleTime0>1000000</CycleTime0>   <!-- 1 000 000 ns = 1 ms -->
  <CycleTime1>0</CycleTime1>
  <ShiftTime>0</ShiftTime>
</DC>
```

The drive is designated **DC reference clock** — unavoidable here, since it is the only slave.

DC is configured by four register writes, all on the **PreOp→SafeOp** transition:

| Register | Name | Value written | Decode |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x09A0` | Sync0/Sync1 cycle time | `40 42 0f 00 00 00 00 00` | Sync0 = `0x000F4240` = 1 000 000 ns; Sync1 = 0 |
| `0x0990` | Start time cyclic operation | `00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00` | start immediately |
| `0x0980`/`0x0981` | Cyclic unit control / Activation | `00 03` | see below |
| `0x09A8` | Latch0 edge config | `00 00` | latch unused |

### The activation value

`0x0980` = `0x00`, `0x0981` = `0x03`.

Register `0x0981` bit 0 is *cyclic operation enable*, bit 1 is *SYNC0 generation*. So `0x03` enables both. This corresponds to an ESI `AssignActivate` of **`#x0300`** — SYNC0 pulses are generated in ESC hardware.

For reference, the other values encountered during commissioning:

| `AssignActivate` | `0x0981` | ENI `Data` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `#x0000` | `0x00` | `0000` | Sync unit disabled |
| `#x0100` | `0x01` | `0001` | cyclic operation only, no SYNC0 pulses |
| `#x0300` | `0x03` | `0003` | cyclic operation + SYNC0 pulses ← **this file** |

Because the drive firmware is polling-based and does not consume SYNC0, enabling the pulses is transparent to it; the sync unit runs entirely in the LAN9252 ESC hardware.

### Master-level DC preparation

Three broadcast writes on Init→PreOp set up the DC drift compensation loop:

| Register | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `0x0910` (32 bytes) | zeroed | clear system time area |
| `0x0930` | `0x1000` (4096) | speed counter start — standard default |
| `0x0934`/`0x0935` | filter depth 12 | system time / speed counter filter depth |

---

## 4. State machine — init command execution

`<Transition>` codes are ordered **source→destination** pairs: `I`=Init, `P`=PreOp, `B`=Bootstrap, `S`=SafeOp, `O`=Op. There is no code meaning "while in state X". The master walks its init command list on every transition and executes each entry whose transition list contains that transition. All 12 master commands carry `BeforeSlave=1`, so master broadcasts precede slave-specific commands within a transition.

Register shorthand used below: `0x0120` = AL Control, `0x0130` = AL Status, `0x0500` = EEPROM assignment, `0x0502`/`0x0508` = EEPROM control/data, `0x0010` = configured station address.

### Init → PreOp (`IP`)

**Master broadcasts:**

1. `BRD 0x0130` ×2 — read slave count
2. `BWR 0x0200` = `0x0004` — enable ECAT interrupt
3. `BWR 0x0010` = 0 — clear configured station addresses
4. `BWR 0x0300` (8 bytes) — clear CRC/error counters
5. `BWR 0x0600` (256 bytes) — clear all FMMUs
6. `BWR 0x0800` (256 bytes) — clear all Sync Managers
7. `BWR 0x0910` (32 bytes) — clear DC system time
8. `BWR 0x0981` = `0x00` — clear DC cyclic unit activation
9. `BWR 0x0930` = `0x1000`, `BWR 0x0934` = filter depth — DC drift loop setup
10. `BWR 0x0103` = `0x00` — disable the configured station alias (second physical address)

**Slave-specific:**

11. `APWR 0x0120` = `0x01` — request Init
12. `APRD 0x0130` — validate Init (`0x01`, mask `0x0F`, timeout 3 000 ms)
13. `APWR 0x0500` = `0x00` — assign EEPROM to ECAT
14. Identity checks via EEPROM reads at `0x0502`/`0x0508`, each with a 100 ms timeout:
    - VendorId at EEPROM word `0x0008` → expect `0x0000004E` (78)
    - ProductCode at word `0x000A` → expect `0x00000001`
    - RevisionNo at word `0x000C` → expect `≥ 0x00000001`
15. `APWR 0x0010` = `0x03E9` — set station address to 1001
16. `FPWR 0x0980` = `0x0000` — clear DC activation
17. `FPWR 0x0800` (16 bytes) = 0 — clear Sync Managers
18. `FPWR 0x0500` = `0x01` — hand EEPROM to PDI
19. `FPWR 0x0120` = `0x02` — request PreOp
20. `FPRD 0x0130` — validate PreOp (`0x02`, mask `0x1F`, timeout 3 000 ms)
21. `APWR 0x0500` = `0x00` — return EEPROM to ECAT

The EEPROM handover at steps 13/18/21 matters: the master borrows the EEPROM interface to read the identity, then releases it to the PDI so the ESC/firmware can use it.

### PreOp → SafeOp (`PS`)

1. `FPWR 0x09A0` — DC cycle time (1 ms)
2. `FPWR 0x0990` — DC start time (0)
3. `FPWR 0x0980` = `0x0003` — **DC activation**
4. `FPWR 0x09A8` — latch config
5. `FPWR 0x0800` — SM0: start `0x1000`, length 20, control `0x64`, enable
6. `FPWR 0x0808` — SM1: start `0x1200`, length 8, control `0x20`, enable
7. `FPWR 0x0600` — FMMU0: logical `0x01000000`, 20 bytes, → `0x1000`, write
8. `FPWR 0x0610` — FMMU1: logical `0x01000000`, 8 bytes, → `0x1200`, read
9. `FPWR 0x0120` = `0x04` — request SafeOp
10. `FPRD 0x0130` — validate SafeOp (timeout 10 000 ms)

DC is armed **before** the Sync Managers and FMMUs are configured, and the state request comes last.

### SafeOp → Op (`SO`)

1. `FPWR 0x0120` = `0x08` — request Op
2. `FPRD 0x0130` — validate Op (timeout 10 000 ms)

Nothing touches DC. The `0x0981 = 0x03` written at `PS` is sticky and remains active through SafeOp and into Op.

### Downward transitions

| Transition | Meaning | DC action |
|---|---|---|
| `PP` | PreOp refresh | clear `0x0980` |
| `SP`, `OP` | SafeOp/Op → PreOp | clear `0x0980`, clear FMMUs, request PreOp |
| `SI`, `OI` | SafeOp/Op → Init | clear `0x0980` (auto-increment), clear FMMUs/SMs, request Init |
| `OS` | Op → SafeOp | request SafeOp only |

Note that `OP` means *Op → PreOp*, not "in Op". The three "clear DC activation" entries are all teardown paths.

### Cold-start summary

On a clean boot the DC registers are touched exactly twice: cleared at `IP`, set at `PS`. Everything else is shutdown handling.

---

## 5. Cyclic frame

```
TaskId    3
Priority  20
CycleTime 1000        (µs → 1 ms)
Comment   synchronized with task 'PlcTask'
```

One frame, four datagrams, in transmission order:

| # | Cmd | Type | Target | Length | WKC | Active in |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | NOP | `0x0900` | 4 | — | PreOp, SafeOp, Op |
| 2 | 13 | ARMW | `0x0910` | 4 | — | PreOp, SafeOp, Op |
| 3 | 12 | LRW | logical `0x01000000` | 20 | 3 | SafeOp, Op |
| 4 | 7 | BRD | `0x0130` | 2 | 1 | PreOp, SafeOp, Op |

**Datagram 2 is the mechanism that keeps DC locked.** `ARMW` (Auto-increment Read Multiple Write) reads the system time from the reference clock slave and writes it to every slave behind it, once per cycle. It is declared active in Op, which is what keeps `0x0981 = 0x03` meaningful during operation.

**Datagram 3** carries the process data: 20 output bytes written, 8 input bytes read, through the shared logical window. Expected working counter is 3 — `LRW` increments WKC by 1 for the read and 2 for the write on a slave that does both.

**Datagram 1** is declared as command type 0 (NOP) targeting `0x0900`, the ESC receive-time latch register. A NOP does not itself latch anything, so this occupies a reserved slot in the frame rather than performing the write its position implies. Worth confirming on the wire what the master actually emits here if precise DC delay measurement ever matters.

---

## 6. TwinCAT process image

The `<ProcessImage>` section maps PDO entries to TwinCAT variables. Both directions declare `ByteSize=1536`.

Process data begins at **bit offset 464** (byte 58) in both directions. Everything at offsets above bit 12160 is TwinCAT-internal diagnostics and never appears on the wire:

- `Frm0State`, `Frm0WcState`, `Frm0InputToggle` — frame-level status
- `WcState` — working counter validity per slave and per sync unit
- `SlaveCount`, `CfgSlaveCount`, `DevState`, `ChangeCount`, `DevId`, `AmsNetId`
- `Box 1 (Drive).InfoData.DcOutputShift` / `DcInputShift` — DC shift diagnostics

`DcOutputShift` and `DcInputShift` are worth watching during commissioning; they report the actual applied shift and will expose a mismatch between the declared cycle and reality.

---

## 7. Observations and anomalies

### ESI defects visible in the PDO map

The TxPDO entry list has two flaws inherited from the ESI:

- **SubIndex 4 is used twice** — both "Thermal protection 1" and "Thermal protection 2" declare `SubIndex 4`; `SubIndex 5` is never used.
- **All entries share one object index** — every TxPDO entry declares `Index #x1` and every RxPDO entry `Index #x2`, rather than each entry pointing at its own object.

Neither affects bit packing, since the master lays entries out sequentially by `BitLen` and the totals are correct (64 input bits, 160 output bits). Both would fail a strict ETG conformance check, and the duplicate SubIndex will confuse any tool that keys entries by index/subindex.

### Padding is explicit

Both PDOs end with an unnamed entry (2 bits input, 24 bits output) to pad to a byte boundary. This is correct practice and makes the 8- and 20-byte SM lengths exact.

### No mailbox

The absence of mailbox Sync Managers is the structural consequence of the drive having no CoE. Any master expecting to run a DS402 startup sequence, read object `0x1000`, or perform SDO-based PDO assignment will fail against this device. It must be treated as a generic EtherCAT slave with a fixed process image.

---

## 8. Comparison checklist

When diffing this against an ENI generated by another master, these are the values that determine whether DC behaves identically:

| Item | Value here |
|---|---|
| `PS` write to `0x0980` | `0003` |
| `0x0990` start time | `0` (8 bytes) |
| `0x09A0` Sync0 cycle | `0x000F4240` (1 ms) |
| `0x09A8` latch config | `0000` |
| `<CycleTime0>` | `1000000` ns |
| `<ShiftTime>` | `0` |
| `<ReferenceClock>` | `true` |
| Cyclic `ARMW` at `0x0910` | active in PreOp, SafeOp, Op |
| `<Cyclic><CycleTime>` | `1000` (µs per ETG.2100) |
| SM0 / SM1 | `0x1000`/20/`0x64`, `0x1200`/8/`0x20` |
| Identity | VendorId 78, ProductCode 1, RevisionNo ≥ 1 |

The `<Cyclic><CycleTime>` unit is the one to watch: ETG.2100 specifies microseconds, so `1000` here is consistent with the 1 ms `CycleTime0`. A master that emits `1` for the same physical cycle is either using milliseconds internally or is genuinely misdeclaring the frame rate by a factor of 1000.
